title: FPS mouse capture / pointer lock for player-mode look
description:
Replace the current click-and-drag mouse-look in DungeonViewerScene's player mode with FPS-style mouse capture: when player mode is active, hide the OS cursor, lock it to the window center, and feed every cursor delta into camera.mouseMove(). Releasing capture (e.g. when toggling to fly-cam, opening a menu, or pressing Escape) restores the OS cursor at its previous position. 

GLFW exposes the needed primitives via glfwSetInputMode with GLFW_CURSOR_DISABLED (hides + recenters automatically; raw delta arrives via the cursor-pos callback). The wrapper lives somewhere in ixdar.platform.gl already (see LwjglPlatform / WebPlatform). Audit the platform layer for an existing setCursorMode hook before adding a new one. 

FlyCamMouseTrap currently gates rotation on left-click drag; PlayerKeyGuy / DungeonViewerScene need a way to swap between 'drag-to-rotate' (fly-cam) and 'always-rotate' (player). Cleanest design: a CursorMode enum (NORMAL, CAPTURED, DISABLED) on the platform, plus a small input-trap subclass for the captured case that no longer requires the LMB-down gate. 

Background: came from real testing — 'I have to click to turn, we should figure out how to capture the mouse'.
definition-of-done: 1. Platform.setCursorMode(NORMAL | CAPTURED) wired to glfwSetInputMode (LWJGL) and to whatever pointer-lock mechanism the WebPlatform supports (probably document.requestPointerLock). 2. DungeonViewerScene calls setCursorMode(CAPTURED) when entering player mode, NORMAL when toggling to fly-cam or shutting down. 3. In CAPTURED mode, every cursor-delta event from the platform feeds camera.mouseMove without requiring a button press. 4. Escape (or another agreed key) cleanly releases capture so the user can click outside the window. 5. Re-entering capture re-hides the cursor without jumping the camera. 6. Existing FlyCamMouseTrap drag-to-rotate behavior unchanged in fly-cam mode.
testing-plan: 1. Launch Ixdar Dungeon Player, confirm cursor is hidden and small mouse motions rotate the camera with no click required. 2. Press F to toggle to fly-cam — cursor reappears at the center of the window. 3. Press F again — cursor disappears, camera capture resumes without snapping. 4. Press Escape — capture releases cleanly. 5. Click back into the window — capture reactivates. 6. On TeaVM/web build, verify pointer-lock works in browser (Chrome / Firefox).
todos: Audit existing platform code for cursor / pointer-lock hooks before adding new ones
Define CursorMode enum on Platform interface (NORMAL, CAPTURED)
WebPlatform.setCursorMode -> document.requestPointerLock / exitPointerLock via TeaVM JSO
Wire DungeonViewerScene mode-toggle (and shutdown) to setCursorMode
Bypass FlyCamMouseTrap's drag-gate in player/captured mode (rotate on every mouse-pos delta)
Manual test on desktop and browser per testing-plan
